vulnerability.title: Rack::Directory's root check uses a raw string prefix comparison, so a path such as /../root_backup/ escapes the configured root and lists a sibling directory before 2.2.22, 3.1.20 and 3.2.5
vulnerability.category_l2: sibling-directory escape via unseparated root prefix match in Rack::Directory (directory listing disclosure)

severity.source: CNA GitHub_M metric and both NVD Secondary metrics (security-advisories@github.com and a CNA-hosted metric) publish the identical CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH vector; OSV GHSA database_specific severity HIGH

fix_commits.message: Prevent directory traversal via root prefix bypass.

The regression test is at test/spec_directory.rb:131.

vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: tag 2.2.3 peels to 1741c580, inside the advisory range <2.2.22; its lib/rack/directory.rb blob be72be0 compares the expanded path against @root with a bare start_with?, and the same blob is still present at v2.2.21

location.verification_method: Static read of lib/rack/directory.rb and lib/rack/utils.rb at tag 2.2.3, the v2.2.21 -> v2.2.22 tag diff, the upstream fix commit and its parent, the regression tests in v2.2.22/v3.1.20/v3.2.5, and the saved advisory records. No Ruby code was run and no request was made.

critical_operation.description: check_forbidden treats any expanded path that begins with the root string as inside the root. Because @root carries no trailing separator, a sibling directory whose name starts with the root's basename (root_test for root) passes the test: File.join(@root, '/../root_test/') keeps the '..', File.expand_path resolves it to the sibling, and start_with?('/tmp/x/root') is true. get() then builds path = File.join(@root, path_info) with the same unnormalised path, list_path stats it and list_directory serves a listing of the sibling, so filenames outside the configured root are disclosed. The fix compares against a root that ends in File::SEPARATOR (or equals the root exactly).

entry_point.description: get() is the Rack application entry point; path_info comes from env[PATH_INFO] after Utils.unescape_path, so a client controls it. Exposure requires Rack::Directory to be mounted in front of a root that has a same-prefix sibling directory, which the advisory states as the precondition.

trace.description: Utils.valid_path? only rejects invalid encodings and NUL bytes (lib/rack/utils.rb:608-610), so a path containing '..' passes this gate
the prefix test accepts a resolved sibling path that merely shares the root string, so no 403 is produced
path = File.join(@root, path_info) keeps the '..' segment; list_path is called with it
stat(path) resolves the '..' on the filesystem; for a directory it calls list_directory, which renders the entries of the sibling directory into a 200 HTML index

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No code was executed and no request was made: the traversal is read from the string check and the file-system path flow, not reproduced against a running server.
The escape requires a sibling directory whose name begins with the configured root's path string; if no such sibling exists there is no effect, and the advisory states this precondition explicitly.
Only directory listing (names, sizes, mtimes) is disclosed for the sibling; the entry does not claim arbitrary file read through this path, though the listing can reveal filenames that matter.
v3.1.20 and v3.2.5 were fetched only to read the regression test; their fix blobs and backport commits were not separately diffed.
No third-party reproduction or analysis was found in the saved sources; if none exists, the independent-evidence field will be false and the entry cannot reach grade A.

Whether an actual Rack server normalises '..' in PATH_INFO before Rack::Directory sees it varies by server; the advisory frames the flaw as exploitable when Rack::Directory is exposed, and the fix hardens the middleware itself.
open_questions: Whether common Rack servers (Puma, WEBrick, falcon) pass an unnormalised '/../' PATH_INFO through to the middleware, which determines real-world reachability.
Whether the same prefix-comparison pattern appears in other Rack path checks (for example Rack::Files or Rack::Static) that this CVE does not cover.

Whether the 2.2.x backport commit has its own hash distinct from the main-branch 75c5745c; the v2.2.21 -> v2.2.22 tag diff proves the content, but the backport commit id was not retrieved because the GitHub API rate limit was hit.
